title: Orchestrator
tagline: Six microservices on a two-node K3s cluster, with StatefulSets, autoscaling and secrets.
summary: A movie inventory and billing system deployed on Kubernetes. Vagrant creates two Debian VMs: one K3s server and one worker. The cluster runs six services: an API gateway, two apps, two databases and a RabbitMQ queue. The gateway and the inventory app scale from 1 to 3 replicas when CPU usage reaches 60%.
problem: A set of microservices had to run on a real orchestrator: keep their data when pods are replaced, scale under load, keep credentials in Kubernetes Secrets instead of the app manifests, and start from a single command.
role: Team of 2. [TODO: what you built, for example the manifests, the Vagrant and K3s setup, or the scripts]
features: One command creates the VMs, installs K3s, joins the worker and applies every manifest: `./Scripts/orchestrator.sh create`
API gateway and inventory app as Deployments with a HorizontalPodAutoscaler: 1 to 3 replicas at 60% CPU
Both databases and the billing app as StatefulSets, with persistent volume claims for the data
Configuration in ConfigMaps, database and RabbitMQ credentials in Secrets
Container images published on Docker Hub
API documented with OpenAPI and a Postman collection

challenges.title: Keeping data when pods are replaced
challenges.problem: Kubernetes can replace a pod at any moment. A database running in a plain Deployment would lose its data.
challenges.solution: The inventory and billing databases run as StatefulSets with persistent volume claims, so their data survives when Kubernetes replaces a database pod.

challenges.title: Scaling with the load
challenges.problem: The public entry point must absorb more traffic without anyone adding replicas by hand.
challenges.solution: HorizontalPodAutoscalers scale the API gateway and the inventory app from 1 to 3 replicas when CPU usage reaches 60%, using the metrics server that ships with K3s.

challenges.title: Never losing an order
challenges.problem: If the billing app is down, orders sent during that time must not disappear.
challenges.solution: The gateway publishes orders to RabbitMQ instead of calling billing directly. The queue keeps the messages until the billing app is back, which then saves them to its database.

learned: When to use a Deployment and when to use a StatefulSet
How a HorizontalPodAutoscaler uses metrics to scale
Managing configuration with ConfigMaps and Secrets
Building a reproducible cluster with Vagrant and K3s
Debugging pods with `kubectl describe` and `kubectl logs`
